PERNIASPOP.why: Weak start: listed 7 September 2026 at ₹535, about 7% below the ₹575 issue price, after an IPO subscribed only 1.29x (non-institutional investors 0.84x). The entire ₹680 crore was fresh capital. The sources found cover listing day only, so there is no explanation yet for later moves.
PERNIASPOP.outlook: No analyst ratings, results or guidance were found. As a luxury fashion omni-channel retailer, the first quarterly results as a listed company will be the test. Market cap at listing was reported at ₹4,300-4,500 crore.

RENTOMOJO.why: Listed 17 September 2026 at ₹482.45, 19% above the ₹404 issue price, on an IPO subscribed 72.9x (QIBs 177x) with Goldman Sachs and HDFC Mutual Fund in the anchor book, and touched ₹534 intraday. FY26 revenue was ₹387 crore and restated profit ₹104 crore, but a brokerage notes the profit was helped by a one-time non-cash deferred tax credit.
RENTOMOJO.outlook: Valuation was the main worry: post-issue P/E about 41x on FY26 earnings and about 98x on FY25. Only ₹150 crore of the ₹1,255 crore issue was fresh (the rest an offer for sale); debt was about ₹258 crore. A brokerage rated it Subscribe for high-risk, long-horizon investors, with asset utilisation, repeat inventory cycles and churn as the key variables.

MPIMANIPAL.why: Listed 17 September 2026 at ₹330, a 2.65% discount to the ₹339 issue price (IPO subscribed only 1.42x; retail 2.19x), after being priced ahead of its only listed peer, Seshaasai (post-listing P/E about 29.5x against 25x). Trading since then has swung widely; snapshots of ₹417 (29 September) and ₹363 (9 October) conflict with the Kite price used here.
MPIMANIPAL.outlook: The IPO funds capacity spending. No analyst ratings or results as a listed company were found, so the stock has to justify its premium through earnings growth. IDBI Capital had recommended subscribing for listing gains.

KARAMTARA.why: Listed 17 September 2026 at ₹320, a 26% premium to the ₹254 issue price, on an IPO subscribed about 63-66x. FY26 revenue reportedly rose 36.5% to ₹4,312 crore and profit 64% to ₹228.8 crore. Of the ₹675 crore fresh issue, ₹600 crore goes to repaying lenders. It makes solar mounting structures, trackers and transmission-line hardware, and is entering wind towers and battery storage.
KARAMTARA.outlook: A research head called it a top pick for listing gains and long-term holding on solar, wind and power-grid demand. Risks: dependence on solar, working capital, customer concentration, borrowings of ₹1,344 crore (standalone, July 2026) and a P/E of about 36x at the issue price. No post-listing results found.

ARMEE.why: Below the ₹375 issue price: listed 30 September 2026 flat on the NSE (₹375) and 1.6% lower on the BSE (₹368.85), then fell about 9% intraday on day one. The IPO was subscribed 2.4x. Over 83% of revenue comes from government and public-sector clients and IT infrastructure is 86% of FY26 revenue. FY26 profit was about ₹45.5 crore (₹41.7 crore a year earlier).
ARMEE.outlook: No analyst ratings, results or guidance were found. Investors will watch revenue growth, contract wins, working capital and use of the ₹300 crore of fresh capital. Government concentration is the key risk.

MONEYVIEW.why: Listed 1 October 2026 at ₹55, a 62% premium to the ₹34 issue price, on an IPO subscribed about 100x (QIBs 227x, non-institutional 115x). The platform connects 140.28 million registered users with 48 financial partners. The ₹1,092 crore issue was ₹750 crore fresh plus a ₹342 crore sale by existing holders; fresh money funds loan disbursals under default-loss guarantees and capital for subsidiary Whizdm Finance.
MONEYVIEW.outlook: No analyst ratings, targets or post-listing results were found. The strong debut reflects demand at listing, not proof of performance. As a lending-linked marketplace, credit quality and its default-loss guarantee exposure are the things to watch.

ACEVECTOR.why: Below the ₹32 issue price: listed 5 October 2026 at ₹28.32 (an 11.5% discount) after an IPO subscribed only 4.9x. It is the parent of Snapdeal, Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands. The ₹420 crore issue was ₹287 crore fresh and the rest a sale by existing holders, and the offer-for-sale was cut before launch.
ACEVECTOR.outlook: No analyst ratings or results as a listed company were found. Unicommerce, one of its units, is itself trading below its IPO price. A later 5paisa snapshot showed about ₹24.6, so the shares have kept sliding since listing.

SRIT.why: Listed 6 October 2026 at ₹148 on the NSE (13.85% above the ₹130 issue price; ₹139.80 on the BSE) on an IPO subscribed 125x (non-institutional 313x), all fresh capital. The Bengaluru IT and ITeS firm serves government and enterprise clients (over 103 projects worth ₹1,235 crore in a decade). It now trades below the issue price.
SRIT.outlook: Proceeds go to expansion, working capital and acquisitions. No analyst ratings, results or guidance were found, and the fall from the listing price is unexplained. Check its first quarterly results as a listed company.
